newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen up with JGBs, Eurodollars await Fed.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen up with JGBs, Eurodollars await Fed.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were higher late on Wednesday on the back of a rise in Japanese government bonds (JGB), renewing dealers' bullish expectations after the market's recent losses.

"Although we've had four days of selldown, it was probably just the market doing a retracement after hitting contract highs. The fundamentals haven't changed," said a trader with a U.S.-based institution.
He said the JGB market continued to be bolstered by outright bond purchases by the Japanese Trust Fund Bureau and the Ministry of Finance.
"A lot of participants are still very bullish and are taking the recent downturn as an opportunity to buy on dips," he said.
He said JGB futures for December delivery were likely to remain supported at 123.35 and breach their contract high of 126.51 before the year-end.
They settled at 124.55 against their previous 124.07.

Dealers said the initial spurt of buying of cash bonds was triggered by a newspaper report of possible financial trouble at a Japanese bank. The Asahi Shimbun said on Wednesday that Nippon Credit Bank's business could be affected by loan guarantees it had made to a financially-troubled non-bank unit.

A spokesman for the bank later denied the report but dealers said it reinforced market expectations the Bank of Japan would be forced to maintain its low interest rate policy to help the ailing banking sector.

"Some players took advantage of the credit bank news to start buying JGBs back aggressively," said a Japanese bank dealer, adding that this had also boosted Euroyen futures. The lead June Euroyen contract was just one tick below its intra-day high of 99.24 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.17. Resistance was expected at 99.25 and 99.28.

Eurodollar futures ended mildly firmer as players adjusted positions ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting later in the day. Dealers said the Fed was expected to leave U.S. interest rates steady as recent economic data had not signalled inflationary pressures.
"Eurodollars could pop up again if the Fed does nothing tonight. The bullish picture is still intact," said a trader with an Asian institution.
He said March Eurodollars could head up to 94.50/52. They finished at 94.46, unchanged from their IMM close.
